fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Madras HC orders TNSTC to reinstate conductor dismissed for excess Rs 7 in money bag
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: The allegations against the sacked conductor were that he did not issue a ticket worth Rs 5 to a lady passenger and was also found having Rs 7 in excess in his money bag. The Madras High Court recently quashed the termination order of a conductor who had been sacked for having Rs.7 excess in his money bag. The conductor had moved the high court alleging that the order of his termination was illegal and arbitrary. He also claimed that the Corporation had not given him a fair opportunity to present his case before his termination. However, the Corporation opposed the plea and submitted that the petitioner was afforded a fair opportunity and it was justified in looking into the past history of the petitioner and therefore the impugned order was not liable to be interfered with. The high court noted that the latest charges against the petitioner were that he did not issue a ticket to a lady passenger after receiving Rs.5, being the ticket amount, and he had Rs.7 excess in his money bag.
